subject: Materials Science
title: Carbon Steel Grades
description: A fast breakdown of Carbon Steel Grades for builders.

hook.text: A car body panel and a knife blade are both steel — but they act nothing alike.

buildup.text: Low-carbon steel (under 0.3%) is soft and formable — ideal for car bodies.

discovery.text: High-carbon steel (over 0.6%) is hard and holds an edge — perfect for cutting tools.

twist.text: Medium-carbon steel sits in between — strong enough for rails and axles.

climax.text: Engineers pick the grade by asking one question: does it need to bend or cut?

punchline.text: More carbon, more hardness — but less forgiveness.

quiz.question: Which carbon steel grade is best for knife blades?
